text:
## Season so far

Walker has been a true workhorse for KC: 22.9 half-PPR points per game and 183.4 total over 8 games. He has carried 159 times for 872 yards (5.5 per carry) and 7 touchdowns. He has added 26 catches for 172 yards and 4 more scores. His season shape is boom-and-bust. He had four games of 20.3 or more (32.6 in Week 1, 30.4 in Week 4, 26.9 in Week 6, 34.3 in Week 9), but also a 7.7 against SEA and a 10.4 against DEN. The pattern is clear: when he scores or breaks a long run he's elite, and when KC stalls he is not a safe floor.

## Usage and efficiency

The volume is real. He has a 74% snap share and 42% of KC's carries and targets (2nd among RBs). He has 34 red-zone carries and 15 goal-line carries, with 9 red-zone and 2 goal-line targets. The receiving role is modest: 15% target share, 4.8 yards per target, and 26 catches that came mostly in short bursts. Weeks 3 and 4 had 2 and 1 targets.

His 11 TDs against 10.8 expected means the scoring isn't lucky. The efficiency is. 5.5 yards per carry is well above the 4.2 RB average, and that number is hard to keep up. Stat Hub puts fair value near 21.5 per game, not 22.9.

Last 4 games vs. the season:
- **Points:** 19.8 per game, down from 22.9.
- **Yards per carry:** 4.7, down from 5.5.
- **Opportunity share:** 39%, down from 42%.
- **Target share:** 13%, down from 15%.
- **Snaps:** flat at 74%.
- **Red zone and goal line:** 15 red-zone carries, 7 goal-line carries and 0 goal-line targets.

The workload is intact and the efficiency is cooling toward normal.

## Health and situation

Walker is Out for Week 10 with a minor groin strain, per ESPN and NFL Network reports in Stat Hub's news feed. He sat out Friday's practice. My own web searches could not independently confirm this. They turned up only old Seahawks-era groin notes, so treat the status as coming from Stat Hub's feed.

Groin strains in RBs usually cost a week or two when minor. They carry a real re-aggravation risk because cutting and acceleration load the area. If he returns, watch for limited practices the week after. A full Friday practice would be the green light.

Emmett Johnson is the beneficiary this week. He has 9% opportunity share over the last 4 games (10 carries, 11 targets, 26% snaps). One search result described him as a modest No. 2 for Week 10, but I couldn't verify his role beyond that. Jaydn Ott (hamstring, questionable) has just 3 carries in the last 4 games. Brashard Smith is on IR, and Ben VanSumeren missed last week's game. Johnson is the clear lead back for the week, but KC doesn't have a proven alternative to Walker. Walker's 39% opportunity share would be spread across thin depth.

## Outlook

Stat Hub projects 169.8 points over the 9 games left, about 21.3 per game after the expected one-game miss. The schedule after the miss is easy: Week 11 vs. ARI is neutral, Week 12 @ BUF is easy, and Week 13 @ LAR is tough. His ceiling is the 30-plus games he has had four times. His floor is the sub-11 games he has had twice, which come when KC's offense stalls and his yards per carry drops.

- **If you hold him:** Treat him as a weekly RB1 once he's back. Bench him this week and stash Johnson only if you're desperate for help, since Johnson's role is unverified.
- **If someone pays for his 22.9 per game:** Sell. Fair value is about 21.5, and the efficiency is likely to keep coming down.
- **Buying:** Not at full price. A minor injury lowers the cost slightly, but not enough to justify chasing him.

Verdict: hold if you own him, sell only for a premium, and check Friday's practice report before Week 11.
